evals.name: knowledge-query-routes-to-playbook
evals.prompt: How should I structure a SKILL.md file for a skill with several reference topics?
evals.expected_output: A skill-authoring answer sourced from the playbook content (progressive disclosure: SKILL.md hub + spoke files). The skill serves its distilled body and does NOT run scripts/update.sh or read vendor/SKILL.md.
expectations: Output answers from the skill-authoring playbook content (e.g. hub SKILL.md dispatches, spoke files do the work / progressive disclosure)
The run does NOT run scripts/update.sh or attempt a drift-check / update action (updating is the separate /playbooks:update skill)
The run does NOT read vendor/SKILL.md for this plain knowledge query

evals.name: skill-tool-one-per-call-and-invocation-reach
evals.prompt: When writing a skill that must run both /toolchain:check and /tdd:principles, and that also needs a plugin's :setup skill first, how do Skill-tool calls work?
evals.expected_output: States that the Skill tool takes one skill per call (two skills means two calls). For a disable-model-invocation / user-invoked-only target such as a :setup skill, does not instruct Skill-tool invocation — tells the user to run /plugin:setup instead.
expectations: Output states that the Skill tool takes one skill per call (a step needing two skills is two calls)
Output does NOT instruct invoking a disable-model-invocation / user-invoked-only :setup skill via the Skill tool
Output tells the user (or the authoring guidance says to tell the user) to run the /plugin:setup slash command instead
